subject: Inference showdown: test plan, success criteria, timeline
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jack Sullivan <jack.sullivan@lumenix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Inference showdown: test plan, success criteria, timeline

Jack — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and a concrete proposal so we can move into an apples-to-apples technical comparison.

Call recap (top priorities you called out):
- Latency (P95 for typical 512-token prompts)
- Unit cost per 1M tokens across realistic loads
- Feature parity: streaming + function/tool calling + structured outputs
- Security/compliance visibility (SOC2 and dataflow)

What Redwood proposes for the technical comparison (high level):
1) Scope: Redwood hosted endpoint (standard) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) vs Hyperscaler endpoints (AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex) and one alternative API (Anthropic-like) provided by your team.
2) Tests: latency distribution (P50/P95/P99), throughput curves (concurrent sessions), cost-modeling using your sample traffic mix, regression checks on a set of 120 representative prompts you provided.
3) Success criteria (suggested):
   - P95 latency < 120ms for 512-token prompts (hosted), < 80ms on Dedicated for same load
   - End-to-end 99th percentile availability > 99.9% during test windows
   - Qualitative: model responses pass your accuracy/guardrail checks on the prompt set (>=90% pass rate by your reviewers)
4) Deliverables: raw traces (token-level latency), consolidated report with cost normalization, and a short runbook for reproducing tests.

Proposed timeline (quick, 2–3 week run):
- Week 0 (this week): agree scope, sign quick-engagement NDA (if needed), share sample prompts + a test account or logs
- Week 1: Redwood sets up test harness + environment (we'll share a lightweight harness repo and detailed run steps)
- Week 2: Execute runs vs each target, collect traces
- Week 3: Analyze, align on results and next steps (rollout plan or procurement)

Owners:
- Redwood POC lead: Evelyn Hart (me) — program lead, scope, customer alignment
- Redwood infra/test lead: Ben Carter — harness + run execution
- Redwood product contact: Vanessa Ortiz — test design, success criteria, quality checks

Attachments: initial test matrix and a draft mutual action agreement for the PoC.
[Attachment: showdown-test-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]
[Attachment: MAA-draft.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

Ask: please confirm the priorities above, add any must-have success criteria we missed, and confirm the internal stakeholders we should loop in (CTO, ML lead, procurement). Also let us know whether you prefer Redwood to run the hyperscaler comparisons from our accounts or if Lumenix wants to run them from your cloud tenancy (recommended for best cost parity).

Hoping we can kick off early next week if that works.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

From: Jack Sullivan <jack.sullivan@lumenix.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Cho <michael.cho@lumenix.com>, Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@lumenix.com>, procurement@lumenix.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Inference showdown: test plan, success criteria, timeline

Evelyn — thanks, that looks great. A few clarifications and must-haves from our side: 

Priorities:
- Primary: end-user latency and consistent tail performance (P95/P99).
- Secondary: total cost (including ingress/egress and model variant pricing).
- Tertiary: ease of integration — SDKs and a clear path to Dedicated if we want to move off hosted.

Stakeholders:
- Michael Cho (CTO) — high level approvals
- Ana Gomez (ML Eng Lead) — will own test verification
- procurement@lumenix.com — contracting and SOW

We also need the following from Redwood before we run anything: 
1) SOC2 report (or SOC2 letter) and a short dataflow summary showing what leaves our tenancy when tests run.
2) Confirmation you can run tests from us-east-1 (we want region parity vs our prod traffic).
3) A short list of what you need from our side (test account, sample prompts — we'll attach an initial set).

On hyperscaler comparisons: we prefer Redwood to run Bedrock/Vertex runs from Redwood accounts for consistency, but we will validate cost numbers from our tenancy if needed. Please include a cost-model normalization step in the report.

We can sign the PoC MAA — procurement will review. Timeline looks fine, but push a couple of buffer days between run and analysis.

I'll attach a CSV with 50 sample prompts to start (we'll follow up with 70 more).

— Jack
Jack Sullivan
Director, Platform Engineering
Lumenix
[Attachment: lumenix-prod-sample-prompts.csv (csv, 15KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference showdown: test plan, success criteria, timeline

Adding technical detail and a concrete runbook outline so we can get Jack everything they need. I'll be the infra lead for execution.

Planned tests (detailed):
- Latency microbench: 512-token canonical prompt, single connection, measure P50/P95/P99 token and end-to-end times
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 concurrent sessions; measure throughput and tail latency degradation
- Cost normalizer: run a fixed token budget (1M tokens) under realistic mixes and produce a normalized $/1M-token metric (includes compute + network egress where applicable)
- Feature validation: streaming latency (first byte), function/tool calling correctness on 30 scripted prompts, structured JSON output validation on 30 prompts

Test harness: lightweight runner (stateless) that hits endpoints with configurable clients. Repo and README: https://github.com/redwood-inference/showdown-harness (we'll open a private fork for Lumenix).

Data & access we need from Lumenix:
1) A short list of prompt variants (Jack's CSV ok as a seed).
2) A test API key for your Anthropic-like endpoint if you want it included (we can also use public endpoints if accessible).
3) If you want hyperscaler runs from your tenancy, an IAM role or short-lived creds (preferred but optional).

Success criteria (operationalized):
- Latency: P95 <= 120ms for hosted during 512-token microbench (pass/fail), and explicit numbers for Dedicated.
- Cost: Redwood equivalent cost <= hyperscaler cost + 10% for same reliability profile (normalized).
- Feature: streaming+function calls pass at least 90% of the scripted correctness checks.

Owners & quick timeline:
- Week 1 (setup): Ben (harness + environment), Vanessa (test design), Lumenix: Ana (prompt verification)
- Week 2 (execute): Ben runs harness across targets; collect traces; Evelyn coordinates stakeholder check-ins
- Week 3 (analysis): Ben + Vanessa produce consolidated report; Evelyn presents results to Lumenix execs

Attachments I'll put in the shared drive: redwood-harness-readme.md, and I'll seed the harness with your CSV.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Lead, Inference Systems
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inference showdown: test plan, success criteria, timeline

Jack / team — quick operational note and a slightly updated schedule now that Ben has outlined the runbook.

NDA/MAA: attached draft MAA should be fine for POC runs (no heavy legal terms). Procurement: can you confirm timeline for review? We can accept a countersigned PDF by Tuesday to keep the schedule.

Region: we can run Redwood-hosted and Dedicated tests from us-east-1. For Bedrock/Vertex comparisons we'll run from Redwood accounts and provide per-run cost details; if Lumenix wants us to execute from your tenancy we can do an IAM role exchange (Ben will follow up).

Temporary access: please provide either a test API key for the Anthropic-like endpoint or short-lived creds for the tenancy you want Redwood to operate in. Ana — can you confirm who on your team will be the point of contact for prompt verification?

Proposed firm dates:
- Nov 8–12: harness setup and smoke tests
- Nov 15–19: full runs across targets (we'll schedule 3 x 2hr windows to minimize noisy neighbors)
- Nov 22–26: analysis and draft report (we'll share a day-by-day artifact set)

If that looks OK I'll schedule the first alignment call for Monday Nov 8 at 10am ET and share calendar invites.

Related HubSpot note for our records: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890 (I'll add timeline there).

— Evelyn

Evelyn / Ben — this is perfect. Procurement will review the MAA and aim to turn it around by Tuesday. Ana confirms she'll be the verification lead and will send a small team.

Two quick questions before we lock calendar invites: 
1) Can Redwood include Bedrock runs using the "bedrock-large-v1" model in the comparison? We want coverage for one managed hyperscaler variant.
2) If we choose Dedicated after a favorable comparison, can Redwood provide an indicative monthly cost for a Dedicated pool sized for ~100 RPS sustained (we can take a ballpark range initially)?

We grant permission to run in us-east-1 from your Redwood accounts for the comparison. We'll attach a short list of compliance questions to the procurement thread. Also, thanks for the SOC2 pointer — please attach a copy when you can.

I'll look out for the calendar invite Monday 11/08 10:00 ET.

— Jack
